newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George surprised by regulation moves.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George surprised by regulation moves.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday he was not consulted by new Labour Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown over moves to reform financial services regulation.
He said he had been broadly aware of Brown's plans to transfer responsibility for banking supervision from the central bank to a revamped Securities and Investments Board.
"It was the timing that was a surprise," he told BBC radio.
He agreed that he had been told of the moves, announced by Brown on Tuesday, rather than consulted. "That's quite true," George said.
"The chancellor had clearly made up his mind. Having made up his mind he decided to act decisively," he said.
George said the Bank of England's position was well known.

"It's not the position of the Bank that's fundamentally important in this. What's really important is whether we have the best regulatory structure for the financial services industry that we could have."
The moves announced by Brown made "a good deal of sense" in that they would protect consumers, investors, depositors and policy-holders.
"Putting it all in once place is a good thing," George said.

He said he was very encouraged that Bank of England staff would initially handle banking supervision in the new SIB and that the agency would be headed by BOE deputy governor Howard Davies. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
